title: Population-resource relationship
competency: Describe over, optimal and under population with respect to natural resources.

keywords.def: The number of people living in a definite area.
Resources that occur in nature, such as soil, water, minerals, wildlife, vegetation and energy sources.
More people in an area than its resources can comfortably support.
Too few people in an area to fully use its resources.
A balanced population-resource relationship in an area.
The number of people a region can support without environmental degradation.
A policy that aims to reduce the birth rate and slow population growth.
A policy that aims to increase the birth rate and population growth.

ideas.name: Population and resources depend on each other

en.text: Population is the number of people living in an area. Natural resources occur in nature: soil, water, minerals, wildlife, vegetation and energy sources. People cannot make them. When population grows or falls, the resources available change. And the resources available affect how population changes.

screens.title: One spring, more people
screens.ask: A village has one spring. Its population doubles. What happens to the water each family gets?
screens.after: More people share the same spring, so each family gets less. Population change affects the resources available.

screens.title: 3.2 Population-resource relationship
paras: Human population is the number of people living in a definite area.
We cannot live without clean air, plants to eat and water to drink.
Natural resources are essential to human wellbeing.

screens.title: Natural resources
paras: Natural resources occur in nature. Humans cannot produce them.
They include soil, water, minerals, wildlife, vegetation and energy sources.
Population and resources have a strong relationship.
Population growth or decline affects the resources available. Resources also affect population trends.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The number of people living in a definite area.
Resources that occur in nature, such as soil, water, minerals, wildlife, vegetation and energy sources.

screens.text: Which of these is a natural resource?
screens.why: Soil occurs in nature; people cannot produce it. Buildings and bicycles are made by people.

screens.text: Tap every natural resource the book lists.
screens.why: The book lists soil, water, minerals, wildlife, vegetation and energy sources. Plastic is made by people.
screens.clue: Which one is made in a factory?

screens.text: The availability of natural resources affects the trends of population.
screens.clue: Does it work in both directions?

screens.text: Why can people NOT simply produce more natural resources when population grows?
opts: Natural resources occur in nature and cannot be produced by humans
screens.ans: Natural resources occur in nature and cannot be produced by humans
screens.why: The book says natural resources cannot be produced by humankind; they come from the environment. So a growing population must share what nature gives.
screens.clue: Read the definition of natural resources again.

en.text: Over population: more people than the resources can comfortably support. It brings low income, unemployment, famine and outward migration. Under population: too few people to use the resources fully; it has low unemployment and inward migration. Optimum population is a balance between people and resources.

screens.title: The balance scale
screens.ask: A balance scale has People on one pan and Resources on the other. The People pan is much heavier. What does this show?
screens.after: More people than resources: over population. If the pans are level, it is optimum population.

screens.title: Overpopulation
paras: Overpopulation is an excess of population in relation to the available resources.
The area has more people than it can comfortably support. Its carrying capacity is exceeded.
It brings low income per person, high unemployment, malnutrition, famine, low living standards and outward migration.

screens.title: Under and optimum population
paras: Under population is the opposite. The population is too small to fully use its resources.
More people would mean better use of resources and higher living standards.
Under population has low unemployment and inward migration.
Optimum population is the balanced population-resource relationship.

screens.title: Key words
defs: More people in an area than its resources can comfortably support.
Too few people in an area to fully use its resources.
A balanced population-resource relationship in an area.
The number of people a region can support without environmental degradation.

screens.text: An area has more people than its resources can comfortably support. This is:
screens.why: Over population is an excess of people in relation to resources.
screens.clue: Which side of the scale is heavier?

screens.title: Which one has it?
items: Too many people for the jobs.
People come to use the resources.
screens.why: Over population brings shortages; under population brings unused resources.
screens.clue: Are there too many people or too few?

screens.why: These are the three book definitions.
screens.clue: Think of the three balance scales.

screens.text: A region has rich farmland but few people, so much land is unused. What would more people most likely bring?
opts: Better use of resources and higher living standards
screens.ans: Better use of resources and higher living standards
screens.why: This is under population. The book says an increase in population would mean more effective use of resources and higher living standards.
screens.clue: Is this region over or under populated?

en.text: Countries use population policies to balance people and resources. An anti natalist policy reduces the birth rate, through family planning education, contraception or law: China and Ethiopia. A pro natalist policy raises the birth rate with incentives: France, Sweden and Romania.

screens.title: What would a government do?
screens.ask: A country has too many people for its resources. What policy would it most likely choose?
opts: Pay people to have more children
screens.after: To slow growth, a country encourages fewer births. This is called an anti natalist policy.

screens.title: Population policies
paras: Over and under population are imbalances between people and resources.
Many countries use population policies to balance this relationship.
table: Family planning education, contraception, or law

screens.title: Do you know? The Chinese one child policy
paras: From 1974 to 1979, China used the slogan "Wan-xi-shao": later marriage, longer gaps, fewer children.
It did not work well, and the population kept growing.
In 1979 China introduced the one child policy. It worked better in towns than in rural areas.
From 1990 it was relaxed a little. It was hard to enforce, and older people became too many.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A policy that aims to reduce the birth rate and slow population growth.
A policy that aims to increase the birth rate and population growth.

screens.text: Which country does the book give as an example of an anti natalist policy?
screens.why: The book lists China, Ethiopia and many developing countries as anti natalist.

screens.text: A pro natalist policy aims to reduce the birth rate.
screens.why: Pro natalist aims to increase the birth rate. Anti natalist reduces it.

screens.text: How does a pro natalist policy usually raise the birth rate?
screens.why: The book says pro natalist policies use incentives.
screens.clue: What would encourage families to have more children?

screens.text: What did "Wan-xi-shao" ask Chinese people to do?
opts: Marry later, wait longer between children, have fewer children
Have only one child by law
screens.ans: Marry later, wait longer between children, have fewer children
screens.why: Wan-xi-shao means later, longer, fewer (1974–1979). The one child law came later, in 1979.
screens.clue: The slogan has three words: later, longer, fewer.

opts: An excess of population in relation to the available resources
Too few people to use the resources
items.ans: An excess of population in relation to the available resources

opts: When the population is too small to fully use its resources
When resources are balanced with population
items.ans: When the population is too small to fully use its resources

items.text: What is the difference between pro natalist and anti natalist policies?
opts: Pro natalist raises the birth rate; anti natalist reduces it
Pro natalist reduces the birth rate; anti natalist raises it
items.ans: Pro natalist raises the birth rate; anti natalist reduces it
items.why: Anti natalist slows growth (family planning, law); pro natalist increases it (incentives).

items.text: How can an anti natalist policy help an overpopulated country?
opts: It slows population growth so people do not exceed resources
It makes the population grow faster
items.ans: It slows population growth so people do not exceed resources
items.why: Slower growth moves the country towards an optimum, balanced population.
items.clue: What is the problem in an overpopulated country?

test.text: The number of people living in a definite area is called:
Under population is characterized by low unemployment and inward migration.
Which is a sign of over population?
test.why: Over population brings low income, unemployment, malnutrition and famine.

test.text: Which country is given as an example of a pro natalist policy?
test.why: France, Sweden and Romania are pro natalist.

test.text: When the people of an area exceed its carrying capacity, the area is:
test.why: Exceeding the carrying capacity means more people than the area can comfortably support.
